text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar signed the draft 1997 state budget, which was afterwards presented to deputies for discussion in parliamentary clubs.

- Annual production of Slovakia's chemical industry totals 82 billion crowns, accounting for about 20 percent of the country's overall industrial production, and for about 25 percent of the industrial exports.
- The government holds its regular session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda does not include major economic items.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Oil refiner Slovnaft plans to create a joint-venture with unspecified partners by the end of this year to build and operate 20 petrol stations in Poland by the year 2000.
- The state monopoly gas distributor SPP said it was interested in stakes of the Czech gas distributors from the portfolio of the Czech privatisation agency, the National Property Fund.

- The net internal debt of the government to the banking sector totalled 59.7 billion crowns at the end of September. Government debt to the central bank totalled 15.4 billion crowns and debts to commercial banks totalled 44.3 billion.
- Textile and clothing company Makyta Puchov said it expected its turnover to total some 1.1 billion crowns this year, compared with 904 million crowns last year.

- Slovakia's major shoe producer JAS Bardejov said it planned to export about one million pairs os shoes to the former Soviet Union, rump Yugoslavia and Bulgaria next year, compared with this year's exports of 500,000 pairs.

SME - DMD Holding, the state coordinator of major engineering companies and arms producers, said it expected to sign a cooperation agreement with Czech engineering firms Skoda Plzen and CKD Praha by the end of this year. Part of the planned cooperation should be investment projects abroad.
